title: VMF target options
description: ADVISOR-1. The target options for every machine in a reviewed assessment, written by the engine beside it (target-advice.json). For each machine: each size series - v5, v6 and v7 - with the facts about it and whether this product supports it, and the option the machine starts on under each of the migration's two defaults. Facts only, as codes; the screen puts them in words.

schemaVersion.description: 33 (TARGET-CAPABILITY-PRECHECK-1, 2026-11-14): the reasons no-encryption-at-host and no-ultra-disk - a size whose catalog entry does not say it supports encryption at host, or Ultra Disks in the zone of the machine (in its region for a machine with no zone), is not offered to a machine the scan found uses it. 32 (IMAGE-SCRIPT-MATCH-1, 2026-11-14): the reason linux-release-not-on-nvme-list - the Linux release of the machine is not on the list of Linux images that Microsoft says support NVMe (data/nvme-linux-releases.json), so it has no v6 or v7 option and keeps v5. 31 (RHEL-EUS-TARGET-NOTE-1, 2026-11-11): each machine says eusImage - the RHEL image on the EUS repositories it was made from, when its kernel for MANA needs a later minor release - so the targets step can say so beside Update the kernel. 30 (SCAN-PARTIAL-SUBS-1, 2026-11-08): the reason sizes-not-read - the scan could not read the size list of the subscription and region of the machine, so the machine is held on every series until a new assessment reads it. 29 (SIZE-FALLTHROUGH-NOTE-1, 2026-11-07): each option says sizesNotTaken - each size the default transform tried before its target size, and the gate that refused it (not-listed, not-in-region, not-approved, gen1-no-size, too-few-nics, too-few-data-disks, smaller-than-source, shape-unknown, one-accelerated-nic), so the targets step can say why the size with a temporary disk was not taken. 28 (REBUILD-REMOVE-PLAN-1, 2026-11-07): the rebuild around the same disks is removed. No option and no size choice has path B; the fields rebuild and identity of each option and size choice, and identityPrincipalId and decide of each machine, are gone; the reason disk-encryption-rebuild is now disk-encryption-preview (and so is that value of burstableTarget); preview says the move is the in-place upgrade (Preview), for Generation 1 too; and the reasons generation-unknown and temp-disk-change-not-measured name a move of a Windows machine across the kinds of temporary disk that nobody measured. The start is the first supported option in the order of the default. 27 (AN-MANA-DRIVER-RULE-1, 2026-11-06): the reason no-mana-driver replaces an-required-no-mana - every size that can give the MANA adapter (every v6 and v7 size, Intel and AMD, Intel v5 and Bsv2) is not offered to a machine whose VM agent reports a Linux release with no MANA driver possible, whether it uses accelerated networking today or not; each linuxRelease says manaUpgrade, the release to upgrade to; the decide reason processor-or-an, its keepsProcessor and keepsAn, and the reason an-intel-v5 are gone, and no option offers an Intel machine an AMD size (2026-11-06). 26 (DRIFT-11-OTHER-OPTIONS-1, 2026-11-05): the reason an-required-no-mana - the target size requires accelerated networking and can give the MANA adapter (every v6 size, Intel v5), and the VM agent of the machine reports a Linux release that Microsoft does not list for MANA. Such a size is not offered. 25 (NO-PLAN-SCOPE-1, 2026-11-03): the reason purchase-plan-out-of-scope - a machine with a Marketplace purchase plan is outside the scope of this tool on every series. 24 (TEMP-DISK-PREVIEW-1, 2026-11-02): each option and size choice says preview - the rebuild of a Windows machine with a SCSI temporary disk, on Generation 2, is offered as an in-place upgrade that needs the preview feature VMTempDiskResizePreview on the subscription. 23 (REBUILD-PICKER-1, 2026-11-01): a machine whose move would rebuild it starts on an option that upgrades it in place, when one loses nothing more (2026-11-01). No field changes. 22 (GEN1-ROUTE-GONE-1, 2026-10-31): the option for Microsoft's route from Generation 1 to Generation 2 is gone, with its move and its reason. A Generation 1 machine has the options v5, v6 and v7 like every machine; the tool has no route from Generation 1 to Generation 2 (2026-10-31). 21 (IDENTITY-LOSS-1, 2026-10-30): each option and size choice says identity - what the move does to the system-assigned identity of the machine (lost, kept, unknown, none) - and each machine says identityType and identityPrincipalId as the scan read them. A machine with a system-assigned identity starts on a target that keeps it where one does, and decide may give the reason identity (2026-10-27: a default never puts a target that deletes the identity before one that keeps it). 20 (HDD-OS-1, 2026-10-25): each machine says osDiskType - the type of its OS disk as the scan read it - so the targets step can offer Standard SSD for an OS disk that is Standard HDD. 19 (DETECT-PATTERNS-1, 2026-10-23): four reasons for workloads outside the scope of this tool on every series - storage-appliance-needs-vendor, managed-application-needs-vendor, shared-disk-cluster-node, sql-availability-group-member. 18 (ADVISE-AN-1, 2026-10-11): each option and size choice says acceleratedNetworking.keptOn and keptOnWhy - whether the accelerated networking the machine uses today keeps working on that size - each machine says linuxRelease and decide (2026-10-11: a machine that keeps either its processor maker or accelerated networking, not both, has no start and a person chooses; its v5 size is the AMD size, marked processorChange, and no Intel v5 size is offered to it - the reason an-intel-v5 where the region has no AMD size; each option says processor and processorChange, and each machine processor), and a machine that uses accelerated networking starts on an option where it certainly keeps working when its default certainly does not and another supported option certainly does. 17 (AN-ONE-NIC-1, 2026-10-10): the reason one-accelerated-nic - after the move more than one network interface of the machine has accelerated networking, and Azure allows it on one network interface only of a size with 2 vCPUs. 16 (DISKS-32-1, 2026-10-10): the reason too-many-data-disks - a machine with more than 32 data disks is outside the scope of this tool on every series. 15 (BSV2-TARGET-1, 2026-10-09): a machine on a B v1 size is offered its Bsv2 size on v5 (sizeChoices family Bsv2), as the best choice and where it starts under both defaults; each option says burstableKept and burstableTarget, and each size choice its own targetStage, stageChange, burstableEnds, burstableKept and prep (pagefile on v5 too, when the size takes the temporary disk away). 14 (AMD-SHAPE-1, 2026-10-09): a machine sized by shape keeps its processor maker - an AMD machine has AMD sizeChoices only - and the reason no-amd-shape-fit says the region has no AMD size of its shape. 13 (GPU-SCOPE-1, 2026-10-09): the reason gpu-size - a GPU size (NC, ND, NG, NV) is outside the scope of this tool. 12 (OLD-FAM-4, 2026-10-04): each option says burstableEnds - the machine is on a burstable size (CPU credits) and its target is not - and the reason size-retired names a size Microsoft has already retired. 11 (DAV4-TEMPDISK-1, 2026-10-04): a machine on an AMD v4 size (Dav4, Dasv4, Eav4, Easv4) goes to the AMD d size on v5, v6 and v7, and its sizeChoices hold that size and the AMD size without a temporary disk. 10 (V3-TEMPDISK-1, 2026-10-03): a v3 machine goes to the d size on v6 and v7, and its sizeChoices hold the d size and the size without a temporary disk on v5, v6 and v7. 9 (OLD-FAM-3, 2026-09-29): three reasons for families this tool does not move - hpc-or-fpga-size, local-nvme-storage-size, l-series-replacement. 8 (OLD-FAM-1, 2026-09-29): the Dl family in sizeChoices, and B v1, F, Fs and Fsv2 sized by shape. 7 (OLD-SKU-1C, 2026-09-29): premiumDisks on each option and each size choice. 6 (OLD-SKU-V6-1, 2026-09-29): sizeChoices on v6 and v7 too, for a Generation 2 machine on an old size, and the reason no-shape-fit. 5 (OLD-SKU-1B, 2026-09-29): each option gains sizeChoices. 4 (V5-ADE-1): the reason disk-encryption-rebuild added. 3 (SIZE-FIT-1): smaller-than-source and shape-unknown. An earlier file is refused by name and made again (Set-VmfTargetChoice, the targets step); nothing is converted.

assessmentHash.description: SHA-256 of the assessment text the options were made from - the same hash the review approval binds.

read.description: False when Azure's sizes for the region could not be read. Its machines then have no supported option.

keptOn.description: ADVISE-AN-1 (v18): the machine uses accelerated networking today, and it keeps working on this size: the operating system drives the adapter the size can give (Mellanox on AMD v5; MANA on every v6 and v7 size and on Intel v5, which Windows and a Linux release Microsoft lists for MANA drive). false: the size gives MANA only (v6, v7) and Microsoft does not list the Linux release for MANA. null: the machine does not use it today, the scan did not say, or the answer is not known (keptOnWhy).

keptOnWhy.description: ADVISE-AN-1 (v18): why keptOn is not true. unlisted: Microsoft does not list the Linux release the VM agent reports for MANA, and the size gives MANA only. image-unlisted: the release is read from the image only, which Microsoft does not list - the image cannot prove the release that runs (an in-place upgrade changes it), so this is not a no. host: the same release on an Intel v5 size, whose host gives Mellanox or MANA. release-unknown: the Linux release could not be read. size-unreadable: the size name could not be read. Null when keptOn is true, or the machine does not use accelerated networking today.

basis.description: stated: Microsoft names the stage. derived: it follows from Microsoft's own definitions.

reason.description: Why an option is not supported. The scan's blockers (data/assessment-reasons.json), the size choice's codes, and the rest.

sizesNotTaken.description: SIZE-FALLTHROUGH-NOTE-1 (v29): each size the default transform tried before targetSize, and the gate that refused it - most often the d size, so the temporary disk goes. Empty when the first size is the target or the size was named.

supported.description: True only when notSupported is empty.

sizeUnverified.description: The size was chosen, but Azure did not report one of the limits it was checked against.

path.description: REBUILD-REMOVE-PLAN-1 (v28): never B - no option rebuilds a machine.

blockers.description: The scan's blockers that apply to this series.

prep.description: The scan's preparation items that apply to this series.

preview.description: TEMP-DISK-PREVIEW-1 (v24), REBUILD-REMOVE-PLAN-1 (v28): the move is the in-place upgrade (Preview), which Azure allows only with the preview feature VMTempDiskResizePreview registered on the subscription - a Windows machine whose move changes the kind of temporary disk, in a shape that was measured: a SCSI temporary disk to an NVMe temporary disk or to none on Generation 2, and to none on Generation 1 (docs/research/temp-disk-in-place-preview.md). False for every other move. The targets step says which subscription needs the feature; Checking reads it before any change.

stageChange.description: Microsoft's lifecycle stage from the source size to the target size. A v4 to v5 move is same.

required.description: Microsoft requires accelerated networking on the target size (Intel D and Intel E v5, and every v6 size).

turnsOn.description: The move turns accelerated networking on for the primary network interface. Null when the scan did not record it, and when the kernel decides: a Linux machine on a size that can give MANA, unless the VM agent reports a release Microsoft does not list for MANA (BSV2-NOTES-1).

stops.description: Stops the engine will make on this option that an approver can clear.

processor.description: ADVISE-AN-1 (v18): the processor maker of the target size (Get-VmfSizeProcessor). Null when the option has no target.

processorChange.description: ADVISE-AN-1 (v18): the target size has another processor maker than the machine - only the AMD v5 size of an Intel machine whose running Linux release Microsoft does not list for MANA (2026-10-11 and 2026-10-12). Null when the option has no target.

premiumDisks.description: OLD-SKU-1C (v7): the target size takes Premium SSD disks (the catalog's PremiumIO). Null: the catalog does not say, which is never read as a yes.

burstableEnds.description: OLD-FAM-4 (v12): the machine is on a burstable size, which runs on CPU credits (the B family, target-families.json burstableFamilies), and the target size is not - so the machine gets full CPU performance all the time, at the price of a size without credits. Null when the option has no target.

burstableKept.description: BSV2-TARGET-1 (v15): the machine is on a burstable size and so is the target size (Bsv2), so it keeps its CPU credits. Null when the option has no target.

burstableTarget.description: BSV2-TARGET-1 (v15): whether a machine on a B v1 size is offered its Bsv2 size on this option (target-families.json burstableTargets: v5 only). offered: a Bsv2 size is in sizeChoices. no-fit: no Bsv2 size in the region has at least the vCPUs and the memory of the machine and takes its network interfaces, its data disks and its generation. disk-encryption-preview (v28; until v27 the move was a rebuild, with a code of its own): the move to the Bsv2 size changes the kind of temporary disk (Windows, from a size with a temporary disk), which the tool refuses to an encrypted machine (V5-ADE-1). Null where the question does not arise: not a B v1 machine, another option, or no target.

sizeChoices.description: OLD-SKU-1B: the sizes on this series a Generation 1 machine, or one on an old size (D v1, DS v1, Dv2, DSv2, Av2), may choose by its shape - v5, and v6 and v7 for a Generation 2 machine (OLD-SKU-V6-1) - and, for a machine on a v3 size (V3-TEMPDISK-1) or an AMD v4 size (DAV4-TEMPDISK-1), the d size and the size without a temporary disk from the replacement table in target-families.json, each with the facts that follow from its size. Only sizes the machine can take. Empty for every other option. targetSize is the one marked best.

family.description: BSV2-TARGET-1 (v15): Bsv2 is offered to a machine on a B v1 size, on v5, first, and is then the best choice.

variant.description: default: the smallest size of the family with at least the machine's vCPUs and memory, or for a v3 or AMD v4 machine either size of its replacement row (V3-TEMPDISK-1, DAV4-TEMPDISK-1). constrained: the same size with fewer active cores, for software licensed by core.

best.description: The size the machine is planned on when nobody chooses: its name twin when the rules give one, else the family that keeps both vCPUs and memory with the fewest vCPUs, D when equal. For a v3 or AMD v4 machine, the d size, which keeps a temporary disk (V3-TEMPDISK-1, DAV4-TEMPDISK-1). For a B v1 machine on v5, its Bsv2 size when one is offered (BSV2-TARGET-1).

targetStage.description: BSV2-TARGET-1 (v15): the lifecycle stage of this size. A Bsv2 size is Current, a D or E v5 size Extended.

prep.description: BSV2-TARGET-1 (v15): the preparation items of this size. A Windows machine whose temporary disk this size takes away has pagefile, on v5 too.

processor.description: ADVISE-AN-1 (v18): the processor maker of this size, by the product's one rule (Get-VmfSizeProcessor). The targets step names it only when one list mixes makers.

processorChange.description: ADVISE-AN-1 (v18): this size has another processor maker than the machine. AN-MANA-DRIVER-RULE-1 (v27): no size choice has one any more - the AMD v5 size of an Intel machine is not offered. Absent on every size choice.

diskController.description: The disk controller the machine has now. Null when Azure reports none (Generation 1).

osDiskType.description: HDD-OS-1 (v20): the type of the OS disk, as the scan read it from the disk resource (assessment osDiskType). Standard_LRS is Standard HDD, which Microsoft retires as an OS disk type on 8 September 2028; the targets step then offers Standard SSD for the OS disk. Null when the scan could not read it, which is never read as a type.

processor.description: ADVISE-AN-1 (v18): the processor maker of the size the machine is on now (Get-VmfSizeProcessor). Null when the name cannot be read.

eusImage.description: RHEL-EUS-TARGET-NOTE-1 (v31): the machine was made from a RHEL pay-as-you-go image whose SKU has a minor version - by Microsoft's Red Hat Update Infrastructure page, an image on the EUS repositories, which give no later minor release - it runs that minor release, and Microsoft's MANA table lists Red Hat only from a later minor release of that major (Get-VmfEusImage). What the scan read: never the repositories the machine uses now, and it changes no offer. Null for every other machine.

image.description: publisher:offer:SKU, as Azure names the image.

release.description: The RHEL minor release of the image, which the machine runs.

listedFrom.description: The lowest RHEL release of that major that Microsoft lists for MANA.

linuxRelease.description: ADVISE-AN-1 (v18): the Linux release the keptOn answers were made from. Null for a machine that is not Linux. The release that runs, from the VM agent (source agent), else the release of the image the machine was made from, which is the lowest it can run (source image). The kernel is never known here: it is read from inside the machine in the run.

distroId.description: The id of Microsoft's MANA table (os-release ID): ubuntu, rhel, sles, debian, ol, almalinux, rocky, azurelinux, centos. Null when no release could be read.

mana.description: Whether Microsoft's MANA table (data/driver-floors.json) lists the release. unknown: no release, Oracle Linux by release (UEK R8 is listed on any release), or an image release whose major release has a row (a routine update raises the minor release in place). AN-MANA-DRIVER-RULE-1 (v27): a release below the lowest row of its major is listed on Red Hat, Rocky and Alma (minorReachedByUpdate): a normal update reaches the row, and its kernel is updated as a listed release's is.

manaUpgrade.description: AN-MANA-DRIVER-RULE-1 (v27): for a machine whose VM agent reports a release with no MANA driver possible, the first release of the same distribution that Microsoft lists for MANA, above it - the targets step says to upgrade the operating system to it, then assess again. Null for every other machine, and when Microsoft lists no later release of the distribution.

identityType.description: IDENTITY-LOSS-1 (v21): the managed identity of the machine as the scan read it, in Azure's own words - None, SystemAssigned, UserAssigned, or SystemAssigned, UserAssigned. Null when the scan did not read it, which is never read as no identity.

start.description: The option the machine starts on under each default: current, the Current lifecycle stage (v6, else v7, else v5), and extended, the Extended stage (v5, else v6, else v7). BSV2-TARGET-1 (v15): a machine whose supported option has a Bsv2 target size starts on that option under both. ADVISE-AN-1 (v18): when that option's acceleratedNetworking.keptOn is false, the machine starts on the first supported option, in the same order, whose keptOn is true; with none, it stays. REBUILD-REMOVE-PLAN-1 (v28): no other rule moves the start. Null when nothing is supported.
